html:
The Cheroenhaka, called Nottoway by their neighbours, are an Iroquoian-speaking people of southeast Virginia, along the Nottoway River. Cheroenhaka is their own name.

Like the Meherrin and Tuscarora, they spoke a language related to those of the Haudenosaunee, unlike the Algonquian Powhatan to the east. They signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation with Virginia in 1677 and kept a reservation in Southampton County, but it was sold off piece by piece in the 1800s. Today the Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) Indian Tribe is recognised by Virginia, though not by the federal government.
